title: Power Automate: direct triggers for desktop flows
summary: The roadmap dates and the documented data-policy path and command are supported. Hold because the page treats licensing without a cloud flow as wholly unpublished despite a general unattended-desktop-flow licensing rule, and rates cost as indirect-only despite the documented desktop-flow consumption meter.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; summary; Why it matters; Open questions
claims.claim: The default state of the roadmap's direct-trigger feature is not stated.
claims.quote: Searched: desktop flows direct triggers licensing pricing default enabled rollout roles; read roadmap, trigger-desktop-flows, console search excerpt and schedule-desktop-flows. No default for this event-trigger roadmap feature found.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model; summary; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: No licensing model specific to the new direct-trigger capability has been published.
claims.quote: Searched: desktop flows direct triggers licensing pricing default enabled rollout roles; opened licensing/types, pay-as-you-go-meters, trigger-desktop-flows and schedule-desktop-flows. General desktop-flow rules exist; no direct-trigger-specific SKU found.

claims.where: controls[0]; summary; Risk assessment; Governance controls; rationale: risk
claims.claim: No tenant or environment UI switch or API for allowing or disabling this direct-event-trigger feature is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: desktop flows direct triggers admin disable PowerShell data policies; opened prevent-data-loss, admin/prevent-data-loss, New-DlpPolicy and schedule-desktop-flows. Per-schedule Enable/Disable is documented, but no tenant switch for this roadmap feature.

claims.claim: Data policies are reached in Power Platform admin center through Security > Settings > Data and privacy > Data policy.
claims.quote: Select Security in the navigation pane. ... In the Security pane, under Settings, select Data and privacy. ... In the Data protection and privacy screen, select the Data policy section.

claims.claim: Microsoft.PowerApps.Administration.PowerShell provides New-DlpPolicy -NewPolicy $NewPolicy to create a data policy.
claims.quote:
New-DlpPolicy -NewPolicy $NewPolicy
Creates a new policy with the $NewPolicy object.

claims.where: controls[1]; Risk assessment; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: General data policies can govern desktop flow modules in an environment and cloud flow connectors.
claims.quote: You can define a DLP policy that manages both desktop flow modules and cloud flow connectors.

claims.where: Governance controls; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: The desktop flow connector can be governed in data policies like other connectors.
claims.quote: The desktop flow connector can be governed in your policies like any other connector in all environments.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Risk assessment; Governance controls; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft has not specified governance of direct triggers themselves or whether desktop flow connector policies govern their triggering route.
claims.quote: Searched: desktop flows direct triggers admin disable PowerShell data policies; read prevent-data-loss and admin/prevent-data-loss. Module enforcement is documented, but no mapping of the new event-trigger route to the desktop flow connector was found.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: The cloud-triggering page identifies the connection creator as the user needing the appropriate licence.
claims.quote: The user who needs to have the appropriate license is the creator of the connection.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Open questions; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The licensing overview says unattended desktop flows require Process licenses or pay-as-you-go.
claims.quote: For additional capacity, running desktop flows unattended, or licensing flows on their own without use licenses, subscribe to Power Automate Process licenses or enable pay-as-you-go.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Whether the same rule applies when no cloud flow is involved
claims.claim: Whether the preceding unattended desktop-flow licensing rule applies without a cloud flow is not yet published.
claims.quote: For additional capacity, running desktop flows unattended, or licensing flows on their own without use licenses, subscribe to Power Automate Process licenses or enable pay-as-you-go.
claims.fix: Replace 'Whether the same rule applies when no cloud flow is involved is not yet published.' with 'The overview states this rule for unattended desktop flows generally, not just cloud-triggered runs; direct-trigger-specific licensing changes have not been published.'

claims.claim: Learn warns to secure a machine and trust its admins before running desktop flows from the cloud.
claims.quote: Before using a machine to run desktop flows from the cloud, ensure that the machine is secured and the machine's admins are trusted.

claims.claim: No approval step for this new direct-event-trigger feature is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: desktop flows direct triggers supported events identity approval frequency limits pricing; opened trigger-desktop-flows, run-desktop-flows-url-shortcuts and schedule-desktop-flows. URL confirmation is documented for another route, not this new feature.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Change & support
claims.claim: No trigger-frequency or run limit for this new direct-event-trigger feature is published.
claims.quote: Searched: desktop flows direct triggers supported events identity approval frequency limits pricing; opened trigger-desktop-flows and schedule-desktop-flows and read limits-and-config search excerpts. No limit stated for this roadmap feature.

claims.claim: The cloud-triggering page documents up to 70 desktop flow runs per minute per connection.
claims.quote: We currently support up to 70 desktop flows runs per minute for every connection.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Open questions
claims.claim: The execution identity and machine-session behavior of the new direct-event-trigger feature are not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: desktop flows direct triggers supported events identity approval frequency limits pricing; opened desktop-flow-connections and schedule-desktop-flows. Existing connection and schedule identities do not identify this roadmap feature's execution model.

claims.claim: No source found states that the new direct-trigger feature changes existing flows automatically.
claims.quote: Searched: desktop flows direct triggers licensing pricing default enabled rollout roles; read roadmap, trigger-desktop-flows and schedule-desktop-flows. No existing-flow migration or automatic behavior change for this roadmap feature found.

claims.claim: The eligible users of the new direct-event-trigger feature have not been published.
claims.quote: Searched: desktop flows direct triggers licensing pricing default enabled rollout roles; opened licensing/types and schedule-desktop-flows. Schedule-owner and Operator permissions describe scheduled triggers, not this identified event-trigger roadmap feature.

claims.claim: Required roles for the new direct-event-trigger feature have not been published.
claims.quote: Searched: desktop flows direct triggers licensing pricing default enabled rollout roles; read run-only-user-role search excerpt and schedule-desktop-flows. No role requirement identified for this roadmap event-trigger capability.

claims.claim: Feature-specific prerequisites for the new direct-event-trigger capability have not been published.
claims.quote: Searched: desktop flows direct triggers event triggers supported configure; opened trigger-desktop-flows and schedule-desktop-flows. Their prerequisites are for cloud triggering and scheduled triggers; neither identifies this new supported-event capability.

claims.claim: Detailed rollout mechanics for the roadmap's direct-event-trigger feature have not been published.
claims.quote: Searched: desktop flows direct triggers licensing pricing default enabled rollout roles; read roadmap and schedule-desktop-flows. Roadmap gives month targets; the regional preview rollout on the latter page is specifically for scheduled triggers.

claims.claim: Microsoft documents a preview Power Automate flow-run meter covering desktop flows in pay-as-you-go environments.
claims.quote: Power Automate flow runs (preview) ... Flow runs for premium cloud flows and desktop flows.

claims.claim: Attended desktop-flow charges in pay-as-you-go environments depend on the running user's licence entitlements.
claims.quote: Attended runs follow the entitlements of the user running the flow. A user whose license includes attended RPA isn't charged; a user whose license doesn't include it is charged $0.60 per run.

claims.claim: Unattended desktop flows in pay-as-you-go environments are charged per run.
claims.quote: Unattended runs are charged at $3.00 per run regardless of any capacity assigned to the environment.

claims.claim: No direct-trigger-specific rate or exception to desktop-flow metering is published.
claims.quote: Searched: desktop flows direct triggers supported events identity approval frequency limits pricing; opened pay-as-you-go-meters and licensing/types. Desktop-flow rates are documented generally, with no exception or rate specific to direct triggers.

claims.claim: Adding desktop flow modules to data policies causes evaluation and suspension of noncompliant flows.
claims.quote: When desktop flow modules are added to DLP policies, your tenant's desktop flows are evaluated against them, and they're suspended if they're noncompliant.

claims.claim: The tenant-level data-policy instructions require the Power Platform Administrator role.
claims.quote: To follow the steps described in this article for tenant-level policies, sign in as a user with the Power Platform Administrator role.

claims.claim: Environment-level data-policy instructions require Environment Admin permissions outside the Dataverse exception.
claims.quote: To follow the steps for environment-level policies, you need to have Power Apps Environment Admin permissions.

claims.claim: Environments with a Dataverse database instead require the System Administrator role for environment-level policies.
claims.quote: For environments with a Dataverse database, you need to be assigned the System Administrator role instead.

claims.claim: Cost is low, meaning indirect cost only, although general desktop-flow licensing and pay-as-you-go rules are documented.
claims.quote: Desktop flow runs in a pay-as-you-go environment are charged as follows: ... Unattended runs are charged at $3.00 per run regardless of any capacity assigned to the environment.
claims.fix: Set cost to 'variable'. Replace the cost rationale with 'Variable. The preview Power Automate flow-run meter charges desktop flows in pay-as-you-go environments; attended charges depend on licence entitlements and unattended runs are charged per run. No direct-trigger-specific rate or exception is published.' Keep licensing.model as 'unknown' for feature-specific licensing.
